fase.key.undertekst: These take the longest. Start here.
fase.before.undertekst: Things you can do while the family is on the way.
fase.week1.undertekst: The most important things right after the family arrives.
fase.money.undertekst: Money from Nav for children under 18.
fase.norsk.undertekst: Next steps once the practical things are in place.
punkt.police.tekst:
The ID number (fødselsnummer) only comes after the police appointment. Without it, a bank account, BankID and much else have to wait.

There are often few appointments available. Many people wait until the family is in Norway, and then the wait is long.

– Read the letter from UDI. It says whether you need to book the appointment yourselves, and who has to attend.
– Book an appointment as early as possible.
– Bring passports and the letter from UDI.

Not sure what the letter means? Call the police.
punkt.postkasse.tittel: Put all the names on the letterbox
punkt.postkasse.tekst:
Letters about residence cards, ID numbers and appointments come by post. If the name is not on the letterbox, the letter may be sent back.

Write the names of everyone in the family on the letterbox, including the children.
punkt.housing.tekst:
It is hard to find a home that is big enough, and the queue for municipal housing is long. Look yourselves while you wait in the queue.

– Look for homes to rent on finn.no. A translation app can help you read the ads.
– Apply for municipal housing.
– Check whether you can get housing allowance (bostøtte).
– Need help with the language, for example to call a landlord? The library can help.
punkt.udi.naar: As soon as you receive it
punkt.udi.tekst:
The letter says when the family can travel, how long the permit lasts, and what the family must do to get a residence card.

– Write down when the family can travel and when the permit expires.
– If the permit can be renewed, you must apply no later than one month before it expires.

Tell the family: «You can travel to Norway from [date]. Bring all the documents listed in the letter.»
punkt.docs.tekst:
Documents can be hard to get later. Bring originals where possible, and take photos of everything. Store the photos somewhere safe, for example in the cloud.

– Passports
– The letter from UDI
– Birth certificates
– Vaccination cards
– School documents
– Prescriptions
punkt.bhg-early.tittel: Apply for a kindergarten place early
punkt.bhg-early.tekst:
Children who live in Tønsberg may have the right to a kindergarten place. Places are allocated by fixed application deadlines. Check the deadline now so you don't miss it.

You need the child's date of birth and the address where you will live.
punkt.police-attend.naar: At the appointment you have been given
punkt.police-attend.tekst:
The family needs a residence card to use most public services.

– Follow what the letter says about who has to attend.
– Children under 18 must come with a parent.
– Bring passports, the letter from UDI and all documents listed in the letter.
punkt.id-letter.tittel: Watch for the letter with the Norwegian ID number
punkt.id-letter.naar: About 2 weeks after the police appointment
punkt.id-letter.tekst:
With a Norwegian ID number (fødselsnummer or D-nummer), the family can get a doctor, a bank account, a school place and most public services.

Most people are registered automatically and get a letter from the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten). If someone gets a D-nummer, or no letter arrives, call Skatteetaten.

Call and say: «My family has come to Norway through family reunification. We have not received a letter about the ID number.»
punkt.bank-id.naar: Adults · Right after the ID number arrives
punkt.bank-id.tekst:
You need a bank account for wages and benefits, and BankID for Helsenorge and many other services. This often takes time.

– Book an appointment at the bank as soon as the ID number has arrived.
– Ask which documents to bring, and bring your passport.
– You can create MinID yourselves on minid.no, but it is not enough for Helsenorge.

Stuck? Call the municipality's switchboard and ask for help.
punkt.tb.naar: From some countries · As soon as possible after arrival
punkt.tb.tekst:
If you come from a country with a lot of tuberculosis and will live in Norway for more than three months, you must be checked. It is required by law, and it is free.

Tønsberg legekontor is responsible and may contact you themselves. If you hear nothing, call them. If you cannot get through, try Re helsestasjon. Bring your passport.

Call and say: «My family has just arrived in Norway. Do they need a tuberculosis check, and when can we come?»
punkt.fastlege.naar: When you have your ID number
punkt.fastlege.tekst:
The GP is the doctor you go to when you are ill, need a prescription or need a referral to a specialist.

– Choose a doctor on helsenorge.no. This requires BankID.
– If you don't have BankID yet, call the GP helpline (fastlegetelefonen).
– Choose a practice near where you live.

People with a D-nummer usually do not have the right to a GP.

Call and say: «My family has just arrived in Norway. We would like to choose a GP.»
punkt.helsestasjon.tekst:
The child health clinic (helsestasjon) follows up the child's health, development and vaccines. It is free and voluntary, but strongly recommended.

Re helsestasjon has extra experience with families who are new to Norway. You can also use the clinic closest to where you live. Bring the child's health records and vaccination card.

Call and say: «I have a young child who has just arrived in Norway. We would like an appointment.»
punkt.vaccines.tittel: Check if the child is missing vaccines
punkt.vaccines.naar: Children and young people · First month
punkt.vaccines.tekst: Some children are missing vaccines from the Norwegian vaccination programme. Bring the vaccination card to the child health clinic or the school health service. They will help you find out what is missing.
punkt.teeth.naar: Children and young people · The first months
punkt.teeth.tekst:
Children and young people get free dental care up to and including the year they turn 18.

The dental clinic usually calls the children in itself, the first time around age three. If the child has toothache, get in touch straight away.
punkt.school.naar: Children aged 6–16 · As soon as possible
punkt.school.tekst:
Children of primary and lower secondary school age have the right to go to school in Norway, and after three months also a duty. School is free.

– Pupils in years 3–10 who are new to Norway can get a place at NOVA at Byskogen skole. Call the switchboard and ask for NOVA.
– Children in years 1–2 usually start at the nearest school.
– Bring school documents from your home country if you have them.

Call and say: «My child has just arrived in Norway. I would like to enrol my child in school.»
punkt.sfo.naar: Children in years 1–4 · Together with school enrolment
punkt.sfo.tekst:
SFO is care before and after school hours. It makes it easier for parents to work or attend Norwegian classes.

Families with a low income may have the right to a lower price. Many do not apply even though they are entitled, so check the municipality's website.
punkt.bhg.naar: Children aged 1–5 · As soon as possible
punkt.bhg.tekst:
Places are limited, and there are fixed application deadlines.

– Apply on the municipality's website, and check the deadline.
– If you need help with the application, you can come to Åpen barnehage.
– Can't apply online, or unsure about the answer? Call the switchboard.
punkt.bhg-price.tittel: Lower price and free hours in kindergarten
punkt.bhg-price.naar: Families with a low income · When you have a place
punkt.bhg-price.tekst:
Families with a low income may have the right to a lower price, and children from age 2 can get 20 free hours a week.

Apply to the municipality and attach documentation of your income. Many do not apply even though they are entitled.
punkt.barnetrygd.tekst:
Child benefit is money from Nav for children under 18 who live in Norway. It does not come automatically – you must apply.

Apply on nav.no/barnetrygd. You need a Norwegian ID number, documentation for the children and your address. Nav can help by phone.

Call and say: «My children have just arrived in Norway. I would like to apply for child benefit.»
punkt.intro.tittel: Check if you can take part in the introduction programme
punkt.intro.tekst:
The introduction programme (introduksjonsprogram) gives training, financial support and follow-up, with the goal of work or education. Whether you can or must take part depends on the basis for your residence.

Bring the letter from UDI and ask Tønsberg læringssenter.

Call and say: «My family has just come to Norway through family reunification. Can we, or must we, take part in the introduction programme?»
punkt.norsk.tekst:
Norwegian makes it easier to get a job, manage on your own and get to know people. Many have the right to free Norwegian classes, and some have a duty.

Tønsberg læringssenter offers Norwegian classes. Bring your Norwegian ID number.

Call and say: «I would like to start Norwegian classes. What is the next step?»
punkt.plan.tittel: Make a plan for work and education
punkt.plan.naar: Adults · When the most important things are sorted
punkt.plan.tekst:
Work or education matters for your finances, everyday life and network.

Nav and the learning centre can help map your education and work experience from your home country, and show you the way forward.
